explanation: Inspect the low bit, add it to the count, and shift right without sign extension. Continue until the remaining 32-bit pattern is zero.
timeComplexity: O(b+1) operations, where b is the highest occupied bit position plus one (b=0 for zero). One shift removes each examined position; b ≤ 32, so worst-case time is constant.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: only a fixed-width remaining value and a counter are retained.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/CountBits.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: After k shifts, the count equals the number of 1s in the k original low positions, and the remaining word contains exactly the unexamined high positions. Adding the low bit and shifting preserves this invariant. A logical right shift introduces zeros, so at most 32 steps exhaust every input, including a negative signed bit pattern.
walkthrough: For x=44 (binary 101100), the remaining words are 44,22,11,5,2,1,0. Their inspected low bits are 0,0,1,1,0,1; adding these gives 3. This implementation examines six positions, even though only three are set.
edgeCases: Zero performs no iterations and returns 0.
The signed input -1 denotes 32 set bits; the result is 32.
The highest bit alone has count 1. The >>> operator, rather than >>, fills with zeros.
